evidence.claim: Through canyons and forests on parts of three historic trails
evidence.quote: The route winds through canyons, farmland and forests and follows part of three historic trails: the Mormon, California and Pony Express trails.

evidence.claim: The Morgan–Parleys drive winds through canyons, farmland and forests, passing East Canyon State Park between Morgan and I-80.
evidence.quote: This drive stretches from I-84 in Morgan along S.R. 66 to East Canyon State Park and then southward along S.R. 65 toward I-80 at Mountain Dell Reservoir. The route winds through canyons, farmland and forests

evidence.claim: Visit Utah gives the trip as 33 miles and 50 minutes and highlights its connections with the Mormon, California and Pony Express trails.
evidence.quote: Morgan-Parleys Scenic Byway 33 miles | 50 minutes

evidence.claim: Utah designated the corridor a state scenic byway on December 11, 2017.
evidence.quote: Morgan-Parleys Scenic Byway (designated December 11, 2017).

evidence.claim: The road’s relationship to the Mormon Trail was deliberate: when SR 65 joined the state highway system in 1931, it followed that trail as closely as practicable over Big Mountain Pass and through Emigration Canyon to Salt Lake City.
evidence.quote: State Route 65 was added to the state highway system in 1931, following the historic Mormon Trail as closely as practicable from SR-5 (US-30S, now I-84) in Henefer over Big Mountain Pass and through Emigration Canyon to Salt Lake City

evidence.claim: In 1969, the state rerouted SR 65 to I-80 in Parleys Canyon and extended SR 66 from Porterville to East Canyon Reservoir.
evidence.quote: The state legislature removed the western portion in 1969, rerouting SR-65 to its current alignment between I-80 in Parley's Canyon and I-84 in Henefer

evidence.claim: From Morgan, SR 66 follows East Canyon Creek through East Canyon, then winds along the reservoir’s northern end.
evidence.quote: Heading away from the park, the route turns northwest as it travels through East Canyon, alongside East Canyon Creek.

evidence.claim: Commercial Street became Morgan’s business center when merchants moved closer to the railroad’s freight and passenger stations.
evidence.quote: Although Morgan's business district was initially located in South Morgan, when the railroad was built, local businessmen saw an opportunity to take business closer to railroad freight and passenger stations.

evidence.claim: Union Pacific laid tracks through Weber Canyon in 1868–1869.
evidence.quote: When the Union Pacific Railroad built tracks through Weber Canyon in 1868-1869,

evidence.claim: Businesses shifted to the west side of the tracks, and Commercial Street remains the town’s main street and the focus of its historic district.
evidence.quote: Commercial Street became Morgan's center of commerce, as many of Morgan's establishments were moved to the west side of the railroad. Commercial Street continues to serve as Morgan's main street and is the focal point of the Morgan Historic District.

evidence.claim: The depot at 98 North Commercial Street dates to 1926 and served passengers until 1972.
evidence.quote: The Morgan Union Pacific Depot, at 98 N. Commercial St. in Morgan, Utah, was built in 1926.

evidence.claim: Ownership passed from Union Pacific to Morgan County in 1982.
evidence.quote: The Depot got transferred to Morgan County's ownership in 1982

evidence.claim: A 680-acre reservoir occupies the narrow-walled canyon at East Canyon State Park.
evidence.quote: East Canyon State Park is a state park of Utah, United States, featuring a 680-acre (280 ha) reservoir.

evidence.claim: East Canyon Creek feeds the water held behind a concrete arch dam built between 1964 and 1966.
evidence.quote: The reservoir is fed by East Canyon Creek and is part of the Weber Basin Project. It was constructed between 1964 and 1966.

evidence.claim: The dam stands 259 feet high and stretches 436 feet across, with a base 20 feet wide and a crest only 7 feet wide.
evidence.quote: is a 259-foot-high (79 m), 436-foot-long (133 m) arch concrete dam. Its base is 20 feet (6.1 m) wide, and its crest is 7 feet (2.1 m) wide.

evidence.claim: SR 66 winds along the northern end of the reservoir before meeting SR 65.
evidence.quote: The route's southern terminus is at its intersection with SR-65 near East Canyon State Park in Morgan County, where it winds to the west along the northern end of the park and East Canyon Reservoir.

evidence.claim: Big Mountain Pass carries the road over a 7,420-foot crossing in the Wasatch Mountains.
evidence.quote: Big Mountain Pass is a mountain pass in the Wasatch Mountains in Utah, United States. It has an elevation of 7,420 feet (2,260 m).

evidence.claim: The Donner Party used it in 1846, followed in 1847 by Mormon pioneers heading for the Salt Lake Valley.
evidence.quote: It is on the original route of the Mormon pioneers who crossed it in 1847 on their way to the Salt Lake Valley. In 1846, the pass was used by the Donner Party.

evidence.claim: When the state established SR 65 in 1931, it kept as close as practicable to the historic Mormon Trail over this pass.
evidence.quote: State Route 65 was added to the state highway system in 1931, following the historic Mormon Trail as closely as practicable

evidence.claim: Snowfall determines the seasonal closure at the crossing.
evidence.quote: The route closes from November to June depending on snowfall in the area.

evidence.claim: SR 65 south of Big Mountain to Little Dell Reservoir closes for approximately six months each winter and spring.
evidence.quote: Note that the S.R. 65 south of Big Mountain to Little Dell Reservoir closes for approximately six months annually from winter to spring.

evidence.claim: SR 66 itself had begun in 1931 as the state connection from Hardscrabble through Porterville to Morgan. The Hardscrabble link left state control in 1953, before the later southward extension brought East Canyon Reservoir into the numbered route.
evidence.quote: State Route 66 was formed on 12 May 1931, connecting the town of Hardscrabble north to Porterville and Morgan. In 1953, the connection from Porterville to Hardscrabble was relinquished from state control. In 1969, the road from Porterville south to the East Canyon Reservoir was transferred from county to state control as a part of an SR-66 extension.

evidence.claim: A steel caboose displayed near the depot once served as a crew shuttle in Ogden before its donation to Morgan in 2019.
evidence.quote: Union Pacific 25822 is a Class CA-11 steel caboose, built in 1979 by International Car, which served as a "snow bus" crew shuttle in Ogden, Utah, before being retired and donated to the city of Morgan, Utah, in 2019. It is now preserved on display near the historic Morgan Union Pacific Train Depot.
